> - `<docs-folder>/changes/<name>/tech-spec.md` — updated technical approach and Code Reference Map
> - `<docs-folder>/changes/<name>/implementation-plan.md` — updated task list (look for `- [ ]` tasks and `⚠️ NEEDS REWORK` tasks)
> - `easyspec-config.yaml` for source paths and conventions
>
> Work through each pending `- [ ]` task and each `⚠️ NEEDS REWORK` task in order:
> 1. Implement or rework the task
> 2. Mark complete: `- [ ]` → `- [x]` (remove `⚠️ NEEDS REWORK` annotation when done)
> 3. Update `tech-spec.md` Code Reference Map with any new/changed code locations
> 4. Proceed to next task
>
> Pause and report if any task is blocked or unclear."

---

## Step 7: Update Tests (Phase B / C / D only)

If the change is in Phase B, C, or D, after the developer confirms implementation is complete, delegate to **es-tester agent** to update the tests:

> "The change `<name>` has been refined. Adjustment: `<adjustment>`.

> 1. **Backend tests** — update/add pytest files as needed
> 2. **Frontend component tests** — update/add Vitest files as needed
> 3. **E2E tests** — update/add Playwright specs as needed. Maintain full user journey coverage per scenario. Use `page.route()` to mock API calls.

> Run all tests. Report pass/fail counts. Fix any failures before proceeding.

> When all layers pass, update `<docs-folder>/changes/<name>/test-plan.md` Test File References with paths to all created or modified test files."

## Step 8: Prepare Demo Cases (Phase D only)

If the change is in Phase D (fully implemented and tested), after all tests pass, prepare demo cases **silently** (no separate announcement):

**If `<docs-folder>/changes/<name>/demo-cases.md` does NOT exist:**
Delegate to **es-tester agent** to create it:

>
> Create `<docs-folder>/changes/<name>/demo-cases.md` with this format:
>
> ```markdown

> <!-- Use with: /demo-app --cases <docs-folder>/changes/<name>/demo-cases.md -->
>

> - Prefer tests that exercise the full user journey for a feature

**If demo-cases.md EXISTS:**
Delegate to **es-tester agent** to update it:

name: es-init
description: Initialize or refresh easyspec for a project — create the root config, confirm the docs folder, and generate code-authoritative master docs
---

Initialize easyspec for this project: create or confirm `easyspec-config.yaml` at the project root, then generate master documentation under `<docs-folder>/master/` that describes the project as the code actually is today. Code is the authority — existing documentation is context, never the final word.

**Input**: No arguments needed. Run as `/es-init`.

**Placeholders**: `<docs-folder>` is resolved from the `docs_folder` setting in `easyspec-config.yaml` (default `easyspec-docs`).

---

## Step 1: Create or Confirm the Root Config (do this first)

This step is mandatory. Do **not** start master doc generation until `easyspec-config.yaml` exists at the project root and is populated.

Check the config state in this order:

1. **Legacy config only** — if `easyspec-config.yaml` is missing but `docs/config.yaml` exists, follow the migration flow in the es-change-lifecycle skill (Step 0 → *Legacy `docs/config.yaml`*). Ask for confirmation, move the config to the project root with `docs_folder: docs`, keep all existing `docs/` content in place, then continue from Step 2.
2. **No config at all** — create it now (Step 1a), including confirming the docs folder.
3. **Config exists but has placeholder values** (any field contains `<` and `>`, or values starting with `TODO:`): announce "Config found but not yet initialized — completing setup." and continue from Step 1a.
4. **Config exists and appears populated**: confirm the docs folder with the user, then jump to Step 2 (Master Doc Generation).

### Step 1a: Confirm the docs folder

Offer the user the docs folder choice and require explicit confirmation. The default is `easyspec-docs`. Explain the choice matters: easyspec will only ever write its master docs and change docs inside this folder, so a folder already used by another documentation tool stays untouched.

### Step 1b: Write the root config

Scan the project structure and detect what you can: project name and description, source code locations (frontend, backend, schema files, test directories), technology stack, project conventions, and domain knowledge. Sources include `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, dependency manifests, and directory layout. Ask the user to confirm detected values and fill gaps in a single batched question.

Then **write** `easyspec-config.yaml` at the project root using this exact structure. Replace the placeholders with confirmed values; keep `null`/`[]` or a `TODO:` value when something is unknown — never omit the file.

```yaml
# easyspec:managed v1
# Easyspec configuration — resolved by every es- agent, prompt, and skill.
# Docs folder: all easyspec content lives under ./<docs-folder>/ (master/, changes/).

docs_folder: <docs-folder>

project:
  name: <project name>
  description: <one-sentence description>

# Source code locations — used by agents to resolve code references
source:
  frontend: null
  backend: null
  schema: null
  tests: []

# Technology stack — context for agents, not prescriptive
tech_stack:
  frontend: null
  backend: null
  database: null
  auth: null
  infra: null

# Key project conventions — agents follow these when making decisions
conventions: []

# Domain knowledge — business rules agents must always know
domain: []
```

The first line (`# easyspec:managed v1`) is the ownership tag and must always be present.

### Step 1c: Verify the config before continuing

Confirm `easyspec-config.yaml` exists at the project root and `docs_folder` is set. If it is still missing, create it now — do not proceed to Step 2 without it.

---

## Step 2: Generate Master Docs (Code-Authoritative)

Generate master documentation for all standard areas under `<docs-folder>/master/`, following the Master Product Docs Structure in the es-change-lifecycle skill — product, architecture, data model, technology, QA, deployment, operations, and reference (as applicable to this project).

**Existing documentation is input context, not authority**:

- Gather any existing project documentation regardless of origin (a legacy `docs/` folder, README files, wikis exported locally, other tools' specs) and read it as context.
- When documentation and code disagree, **the code wins**. Verify claims against the actual source before writing them into master docs.
- Never modify or delete existing documentation from other sources — treat it read-only.

**When no usable documentation exists** (or it is contradicted by the code), scan the codebase directly:

- Inspect project structure, the source locations listed in `easyspec-config.yaml`'s `source` section, dependency manifests, and test layout.
- Derive master docs from what the code actually does: entry points, modules, data entities, tech stack, test strategy, deployment and operations signals (CI configs, containers, infrastructure files).

**Graceful degradation**: when code structure cannot be reliably detected (e.g. an unfamiliar layout, monorepo with mixed conventions), stop and ask the user rather than guessing. A wrong path in a master doc is worse than an unset one.

# Ownership Tag Contract & `easyspec-config.yaml` Schema

## Ownership Tag Contract

### Safety rule (must never be violated)

> **Untagged files are never deleted.** Neither init nor the upgrade flow will ever delete
> or overwrite a file that does not carry the easyspec ownership tag — including user files
> that share a name with an easyspec artifact.

### Tag format

The tag is a stable, version-carrying marker embedded as a comment so it survives in any
text-based artifact format (markdown, YAML, HTML):

```
<!-- easyspec:managed v1 -->
```

- **Marker core**: the substring `easyspec:managed v1`.
- **Detection** is a plain substring match on the marker core, so it works regardless of
  the target tool's wrapper format (copilot `.prompt.md`, opencode/claude-code command
  `.md`, skill `SKILL.md`, generated master/change docs, YAML config).
- **YAML files** use the same marker core in a YAML comment form:
  `# easyspec:managed v1`.
- **Version stability**: the `v1` suffix is part of the contract. Future releases that
  change the tag scheme must still recognize `easyspec:managed v1` artifacts so upgrades
  remain safe across versions.

### Where the tag is required

Every artifact easyspec creates for users:

- The root `easyspec-config.yaml` (YAML comment form).
- Generated master docs (`<docs-folder>/master/**`) and change docs
  (`<docs-folder>/changes/**`) created by `es-init` and the change lifecycle.
- Installed prompts, agents, and skills (HTML-comment form, appended to rendered output —
  the tag survives the per-target-tool template transformation because it is applied after
  rendering, at write time).

### Who consumes the tag

The installer's upgrade-cleanup logic. A file becomes a deletion candidate only when ALL
of the following hold:

1. It appears in the previous install manifest **or** matches a known retired artifact
   name (e.g. `es-change-init`).
2. It is no longer produced by the new version.
3. It is verified to carry the ownership tag on disk.

Even then, the user is asked to confirm each deletion and may keep any file.

## Install Manifest

- Location: `.easyspec/manifest.json` **inside the installed tool directory** —
  e.g. `<workspace>/.github/.easyspec/manifest.json` (project scope) or
  `~/.copilot/.easyspec/manifest.json` (global scope).
- Contents: manifest format version, install timestamp, and the list of installed files
  (paths relative to the tool directory) each with a content hash.
- Written after every real (non-`--dry-run`) install; `--dry-run` never writes it.

## `easyspec-config.yaml` Schema

Location: project root. Single authoritative easyspec configuration; all agents, prompts,
skills, and CLI code resolve paths from it.

```yaml
# easyspec:managed v1
# Easyspec configuration — resolved by every es- agent, prompt, and skill.

# Docs folder: where all easyspec project content lives (master docs, change docs).
docs_folder: easyspec-docs

project:
  name: <project name>
  description: <one-sentence description>

# Source code locations — used by agents to resolve code references
source:
  frontend: null
  backend: null
  schema: null
  tests: []

# Technology stack — context for agents, not prescriptive
tech_stack:
  frontend: null
  backend: null
  database: null
  auth: null
  infra: null

# Key project conventions — agents follow these when making decisions
conventions: []

# Domain knowledge — business rules agents must always know
domain: []
```

- `docs_folder` default: `easyspec-docs`. Confirmed with the user during init (installer
  or `es-init`); the confirmed value is written here.
- The remaining sections carry over the project context previously stored in the legacy
  `docs/config.yaml`.
- Derived paths: master docs at `<docs-folder>/master/`, change docs at
  `<docs-folder>/changes/`.

## Legacy layout caveat

Projects initialized with the old hardcoded `docs/` layout (e.g. `docs/config.yaml`,
`docs/master/`, `docs/changes/`) are **not** migrated by this change. They require a
one-time manual re-init: run init / `/es-init` again, confirm the docs folder, and move
or re-generate master docs under the configured folder. The easyspec source repo itself
keeps its historical `docs/changes/` content in place for reference.

# PRD: easyspec-config-and-init-rework

## Epic Overview

Easyspec currently hardcodes `docs/` as the folder where all of its product documentation lives, and its entry-point command `es-change-init` is misleadingly named — it initializes the whole project for easyspec, not an individual change. When teams adopt easyspec in a project that already has a `docs/` folder managed by another tool or kit, easyspec collides with, overrides, or mixes into those existing documents, making adoption risky and cleanup painful. This epic reworks adoption and configuration: the docs folder becomes user-configurable via a root-level `easyspec-config.yaml`, the init command is renamed to `es-init`, initialization generates master documentation that reflects the actual current state of the codebase, and every easyspec-owned artifact carries an ownership tag so upgrades can safely remove obsolete files without ever touching files easyspec does not own. Together these changes make easyspec safe to adopt in existing projects and

# Feature: Configurable Docs Folder

Easyspec must never assume where a project's documentation lives. The docs location is a per-project choice, recorded once and honored everywhere.

## Capability

- During project initialization, the user chooses the folder easyspec uses for all of its project documentation; a sensible default (`easyspec-docs`) is offered and the choice is confirmed before anything is created.
- The confirmed choice is recorded in a single authoritative root-level configuration file (`easyspec-config.yaml`) at the project root.
- All easyspec project content — configuration, master documentation, and change documentation — lives under the configured folder.
- All easyspec tooling (agents, prompts, skills, installer) resolves documentation paths from that configuration; no component relies on a hardcoded documentation location.
- Existing documentation from any other tool or convention is never touched: easyspec simply works alongside it in its own folder.

## Value

- Teams can adopt easyspec in projects that already use other documentation tooling with zero risk of collision or overwrite.
- One authoritative configuration removes ambiguity for both humans and the distributed agent team about where documentation lives.

## Rules

- Initialization always presents and confirms the docs-folder choice; the default is accepted by simply confirming.
- No easyspec-generated project content is ever written outside the configured docs folder.
- Configuration is a single root-level file; multiple docs folders or nested configurations per project are not supported.
- Legacy `docs/config.yaml` projects migrate in one confirmed step: the config moves to the root with `docs_folder: docs`; existing docs content is left in place.

## Out of Scope

- Automatic migration of existing documentation content into a different docs folder (only the legacy config file is moved, with confirmation).
- Non-YAML configuration formats or environment-variable-based configuration.

<!-- easyspec:managed v1 -->
# Feature: Project Initialization (es-init)

`es-init` is the single entry point for bringing easyspec into a project. Its name reflects its purpose: it initializes the project for easyspec, not an individual change.

## Capability

- Running `es-init` performs the full adoption flow in one guided step:
  - Creates the root-level easyspec configuration file.
  - Confirms the docs-folder choice with the user (default `easyspec-docs`).
  - Generates the complete set of master documentation describing the project's current state.
  - Tags every created artifact as easyspec-owned.
- Master documentation is grounded in the code, not in stale prose:
  - Existing project documentation (from any source) is used as input context when present.
  - When documentation and code disagree, the generated docs follow the code.
  - When no usable documentation exists, the codebase itself is scanned to produce the docs.
- Master docs cover the standard areas (product, architecture, data model, technology, QA, deployment, operations, reference as applicable).

# Feature: Ownership Tagging & Safe Upgrades

Every artifact easyspec creates is explicitly marked as easyspec-owned, making the kit safe to upgrade and safe to remove — without ever endangering user files.

## Capability

- Every user-facing artifact easyspec creates — master docs, change docs, the root config file, and installed prompts/agents/skills — carries a machine-readable easyspec ownership marker.
- The marker is stable across versions so future upgrades can identify artifacts created by this and earlier releases.
- On version upgrade, the installer:
  - Identifies obsolete easyspec files from previous versions **by their retired name only** (`es-change-init`, `es-change-review`) as deletion candidates.
  - Presents each deletion candidate for user confirmation, with a per-file or batched option to keep any old file.
  - Skips declined deletions without error.
- Files other than known retired artifacts — including user files that happen to share an `es-` name — are never deleted or overwritten.

## Value

- Upgrades become a single guided step with zero risk to user-authored content: stale kit files are cleaned up, user files are untouchable.
- The kit is self-describing: automated lifecycle operations (cleanup, migration, upgrade) need no user bookkeeping about which files easyspec owns.

## Rules

- Ownership tagging is mandatory for every easyspec-created artifact, in every target tool's format.
- Untagged files are categorically excluded from automatic deletion; only files matching a known retired artifact name are offered for deletion, after confirmation.
- All deletions are confirm-by-default; unattended automatic upgrades are out of scope.

# Module: Installer / CLI

The CLI installer is easyspec's entry point into a project. It installs the kit into the user's target AI tool and manages upgrades.

## Responsibilities

- **Config scaffolding** — on init, when no root config exists, writes `easyspec-config.yaml` at the project root and prompts the user to confirm or change the docs-folder name (default `easyspec-docs`). No hardcoded `docs/` path remains; every written path derives from the confirmed docs folder.
- **Artifact installation** — installs prompts, agents, and skills per target tool, embedding the easyspec ownership tag in every created or transformed file.
- **Upgrade cleanup** — offers to delete files whose names match a known retired artifact (e.g. `es-change-init`, `es-change-review`), each confirmed by the user with a keep option. Nothing else is treated as a deletion candidate — current files and user files are left untouched.
- **Legacy uninstall** — detects and removes retired artifacts (e.g. `es-change-init`, `es-change-review`) from upgrades of older versions, via the same confirmation flow. Cleanup and manifest recording run per distinct install root (including Copilot's global prompts directory).

## Context

```mermaid

    U[User] --> I[Installer]
    I --> C[easyspec-config.yaml]
    I --> T[Template Transformation Pipeline]
    T --> A[Tagged Installed Artifacts]
    I --> M[Version Manifest]
    A --> U2[Upgrade Cleanup]
    M --> U2
    U2 --> U
```

## Key Behaviors

- All paths resolve from the configured docs folder, never hardcoded.
- Tagging must survive per-target-tool transformation since there is no build step.
- The ownership tag format is version-stable so cleanup recognizes artifacts from earlier versions.
- Declined deletions are skipped without error.

# Module: Upgrade Cleanup

Upgrade cleanup keeps a project's installed easyspec artifacts in sync with the current kit version, without ever destroying user content.

## Responsibilities

- Walk the installed easyspec directories for files whose name matches a known retired artifact (`RETIRED_ARTIFACT_PATTERNS`).
- Identify **deletion candidates**: only files matching a retired name (such as `es-change-init` and `es-change-review`).
- Present each candidate for user confirmation, with a per-file or batched keep option.
- Skip declined deletions without error.

## Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Upgrade starts] --> B[Walk installed files]
    B --> C{Name matches a retired artifact?}
    C -->|Yes| D[Deletion candidate]
    C -->|No| E[Never touched]
    D --> F{User confirms?}
    F -->|Delete| G[Removed]
    F -->|Keep| H[Skipped without error]
```

## Safety Contract

- The only files easyspec ever offers to delete are those whose names match a known retired artifact (`es-change-init`, `es-change-review`). Everything else — current files, user files, and other `es-*` files — is never deleted or overwritten.
- The ownership tag format is version-stable, so future releases recognize artifacts tagged by earlier versions.
- Legacy uninstall (e.g. removing `es-change-init`/`es-change-review` artifacts from older installs) reuses the same name matching and confirmation.
